title: Circular Movements in the Occipital Area
summary: The finger pads make very small, slow circles over the soft tissues just below the occipital line.
goal: Gently mobilize superficial soft tissues in the occipital region without deep focal pressure.
imageAlt: Educational diagram of small circular movements in the occipital area.
startingPosition: The head is supported. The fingers rest on soft tissue below the occipital bone rather than on the bone itself.
instructions: Place the finger pads on soft tissue below the occipital line.
Make small, slow circles that move with the tissue.
Move to a nearby area and repeat.
Work symmetrically on both sides of the midline.
direction: Small local circles below the occipital line.
tips: Reduce pressure immediately if discomfort appears.
mistakes: Sliding over the hair instead of moving the soft tissue.
warning: Do not perform after a recent head or neck injury or with marked dizziness, neurological symptoms, or unexplained severe headache.
telegramCaption: Small, slow circles over the soft tissues below the occipital line.
